# After a header reorder the overflow plugin hides every tab for ~65 ms

## Context

Ada's 2026-10-10 03:55Z defect-note: `DockTabReorderGesture` › "a click after a reorder activates the item its button shows" is flaky on dev `5698517f19` (dev 2/18, the #19538 branch 4/30): the header re-renders ~110 ms after the drop and the click lands on the toolbar. The operator's v13.2 cut order ([#14800, 6097885253](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-6097885253)) lists it under dock polish. Measured here at dev `5698517f19` on `examples/dashboard/dock`, headless Chromium 1600×1000: five runs, identical timelines.

## The Problem

After a within-header reorder (Swarm dragged behind Timeline) the strip collapses to the active tab plus a "…" overflow control, then recovers:

| ms after mouseup | main thread |
|---|---|
| 27 | the reorder's own deltas: `moveNode` for the two shifted buttons (a move, not a re-render) |
| 60–63 | the overflow plugin's post-drag pass measures `extent 0` and decides to hide 6 of 7 tabs |
| 78 | `insertNode` of the overflow control (`neo-tab-overflow-control`) into the rail |
| 94–96 | `removeNode` for the six inactive tab buttons; the strip shows SWARM and "…" |
| 97–131 | `neo-dashboard-dock-animating` is **absent**: the spec's rest signal reads "at rest" while six buttons are gone |
| 149–162 | the next pass measures `extent 692`, re-inserts the six buttons and hides the control |

Paint witnesses (the strip clipped at +40 and +100 ms) show only SWARM and "…"; at +300 ms all seven tabs. On a 60 Hz display that is three to four blank frames at every reorder, and a pointer that lands in the window hits the toolbar instead of a button, which is the flake.

## The Architectural Reality

- The drag's `mousedown` focuses the tab button, so `toolbar.Base#applyContextualActionState` (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:245`, gated on `containsFocus` at `:370-376`) brings the dock header's four contextual actions back: the header's action set grows from one item to four. Their DOM nodes land at ~68–78 ms.
- `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow#project` (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:815-841`) measures the owner, every action item and the control in one `getDomRect` round trip, derives `actionStart` from `actionRects[0]` (`:822`), takes `coordinateExtent = actionStart − ownerStart` (`:829`) and `extent = min(coordinateExtent, sizeExtent)` (`:839-841`).
- The post-drag pass (`scheduleSortDragProjection`, `:552`, drains as soon as the SortZone's `dragEndActive` clears) runs at ~60 ms. The first action item is in `items` but not in the DOM yet, so its rect is all zeros: `actionStart = 0`, `coordinateExtent = 0`, `extent = 0` while `sizeExtent` is 752. `computeOverflow` hides everything but the protected active tab (`hidden: 6`), `applySplit` removes the six buttons, `syncControl` inserts the control.
- The pass publishes `overflowProjectionStart` / `Idle` around its own work (`:591-608`; the dock adapter maps the pair to `MotionSignal` at `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1296-1297`), so after it lands the signal is idle while the wrong split is painted.

Design authority: `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:834-838` — "Visible tabs can briefly push the action rail beyond the owner after a wide→narrow resize. Its coordinate then overstates available space and self-sustains an all-visible split. The rendered action widths provide the owner-bounded ceiling; the coordinate remains authoritative whenever gaps, margins, or another stricter boundary make it smaller." The measured case falls outside that premise: the "stricter boundary" is a node that has no box yet, an absent measurement rather than a boundary.

## The Fix

In `Overflow#project`, derive `actionStart` from the first action rect with a positive main-axis size, and let `coordinateExtent` fall back to `null` (the existing `sizeExtent` path) when no action rect is laid out. `actionSize` already clamps unlaid-out rects to 0 (`:823-827`), so the size path is right for them; only the coordinate path trusts an all-zero rect. No change to `computeOverflow`, the drain, the dock reconciler or the spec's rest signal.

Red-first unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/tab/plugin/Overflow.spec.mjs`: a pass whose first action rect is `{x: 0, width: 0}` on a 772-wide owner keeps every tab visible; the same pass with a laid-out first action at x 692 still caps at 692 (the control for the existing split arms). Then `DockTabReorderGesture.spec.mjs` ×10 interleaved on dev and at the head, Ada's method.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `Overflow#project` ignores action rects with no main-axis size when deriving `coordinateExtent`; with none laid out, the size path decides.
- [ ] AC-2: the red-first unit arm is red on dev and green at the head; the existing Overflow arms stay green.
- [ ] AC-3: on `examples/dashboard/dock`, after the reorder gesture no tab button leaves the DOM and no overflow control is inserted (the delta log shows only the two `moveNode`s).
- [ ] AC-4: `DockTabReorderGesture` "a click after a reorder" 10/10 at the head, the dev baseline rate recorded beside it.

## Out of Scope

- The motion signal's gap between a pass that applied a split and the pass that corrects it: with AC-1 no wrong split lands on this path. Another transient geometry reaching the plugin is a separate ticket.
- Making the post-drag drain wait for the header's pending action commit. Rejected as the first shape: it would still trust a zero rect from any other source, and the drain's JSDoc wants the first pass after the drop.
- Ada's second note (the place-cycle restore ~12 px off baseline): environment, unowned.

## Avoided Traps

- Reading `restingTab` as the defect: the spec's wait is right; the DOM it waits on is wrong for ~65 ms with no signal.
- Blaming the dock reconciler: the retained toolbar is reparented into the new shell at ~127 ms, after the buttons are gone; the reconciler's post-swap `project(true)` (#19094) is the pass that restores them.
- Blaming the reorder's vdom update: the 27 ms batch moves the two shifted buttons by id, as #18652 designed.
